venue_now: preprint: arXiv 2508.00831v2, 11 Aug 2025, marked 'Preprint.' (p.1); no venue in the text
what_it_is: EngiBench (Felten et al.) is an open-source Python library and set of datasets for data-driven engineering design optimisation, that is, machine-learning methods such as inverse design with generative models and surrogate-based optimisation (pp.1-3, 5). Each problem pairs a physics simulator with a dataset of designs, conditions and objectives behind a unified API with constraint checking and adjoint optimisers (pp.5-6). It ships seven problems: airfoil, 2D and 3D heat conduction, thermoelastic beams, beams, photonics and power electronics (Table 1, p.7). A companion library, EngiOpt, provides GAN, diffusion and MLP+NSGA-II baselines, which proof-of-concept experiments compare using MMD, DPP diversity, the cumulative optimality gap and the ratio of violated constraints (pp.3-4, 8-9). It evaluates no language model.
domain: engineering design optimisation for machine learning: aerodynamics, thermal diffusion, structural topology, photonics, power electronics (Table 1, p.7)
size: 7 design problems, each with a simulator and dataset (Table 1, p.7); dataset sizes vary by problem (e.g. an airfoil split of 748/140/47 samples, p.21); 3 generative models compared across problems plus specialised baselines (pp.8-9)
source_of_items: simulation-generated design datasets; several problems replicate setups from prior publications (pp.6-7)
instances: static datasets generated by simulators; the API can generate more data (p.6)
evaluation: machine-learning and optimisation metrics on generated designs: MMD (similarity), DPP (diversity), cumulative optimality gap, ratio of violated constraints, ratio of failed simulations (pp.3-4, 8-9); no language-model or reasoning evaluation
human_validation: none relevant: there are no human-labelled items and no evaluator validation; the problem implementations follow published setups (pp.6-7)

engtrace_use.sentence: Not cited in the text and absent from the reference list. It is named only in a note inside the Zhou et al. 2025 entry (L1248-1249): 'Distinct from the design-focused EngiBench by Felten et al.'
engtrace_use.explanation: The note's description is right: Felten et al.'s EngiBench is 'A Framework for Data-Driven Engineering Design Research' (p.1), a library for benchmarking machine-learning design-optimisation methods (pp.1-2), unrelated to Zhou et al.'s LLM benchmark of the same name. The problem is form, not content. A reference entry should not carry a note naming a second work that has no entry of its own (citation map C15g). The name clash also does not need resolving in an LLM-benchmark paper, because the text always cites 'EngiBench (Zhou et al., 2025)' and the entry's title says what the benchmark is.

suggested_wording: Only if the authors keep the disambiguation, as a footnote with its own reference entry: 'Not to be confused with EngiBench (Felten et al., 2025), a library of engineering design-optimisation problems and datasets for benchmarking machine-learning methods such as generative and surrogate models, which does not evaluate language models.'
facts_to_cite: An open-source library and datasets for data-driven engineering design, with a unified API (pp.1-2, 5)
Seven problems, each with a simulator and dataset: Airfoil, HeatConduction2D/3D, ThermoElasticBeams2D, Beams2D, Photonics2D and PowerElectronics (Table 1, p.7)
Baselines in the companion EngiOpt library: GANs, diffusion models and MLP+NSGA-II (p.8)
Metrics: MMD, DPP diversity, cumulative optimality gap, ratio of violated constraints and ratio of failed simulations (pp.3-4)
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares only the engineering domain, physics-based verification by simulators, and the name 'EngiBench'. Lacks everything EngTrace is about: it is not a language-model or reasoning benchmark, and it has no natural-language problems, generated question instances, gold traces, step-level evaluation or validation of an evaluator against experts.
notes: The naming clash is real: Felten et al.'s arXiv id (2508.00831, p.1) is earlier than Zhou et al.'s (2509.17677, zhou2025engibench p.1), so a search for 'EngiBench' may find Felten et al. first. Even so, a careful reviewer of EngTrace would not expect it to be cited, as it evaluates no language model. Recommendation: remove the note from the Zhou entry, and add a proper entry only if a disambiguating footnote is kept.
